audit.whatIsWrong: Levels 1-2 were given to Graves/Skill while whys[0] and whys[1] say Karma chunks him freely with no level-1 answer, and 2+ items was given to Graves while whys[6] and spikes[3] say Karma reclaims that window.
audit.why: Packet levelChart is Karma, Karma, Skill, Skill, Skill, Skill, Karma and the graves__karma mirror was already flipped as one atomic group to exactly that. Karma's Q is 950 with Mantra live at level 1; Quickdraw is a 425 dash he does not have until level 3.
audit.corrected: Rows 0,1 -> Karma; rows 2,3 -> Skill; row 6 -> Karma, proposed as matched full/content pairs in one atomic group.
sources: kits: Karma Q 950, Graves E range 425

audit.whatIsWrong: The 2+ items phase read as generic 'drift toward utility' with no statement of why that stage belongs to Karma.
audit.why: Graves builds as a tanky ADC and fades as a solo threat while Karma's Mantra-E and Mantra-W keep scaling as teamfight utility; the mirror already restated her window as level 1 onward with Mantra empowering the ability she casts next, not a level-6 unlock.
audit.corrected: phases[6].why now names the Mantra-E shield and Mantra-W heal as the reason the stage is hers.
sources: kit: Karma E and W Mantra bonuses

audit.whatIsWrong: Smoke Screen is described as a blind in whys[2], spikes[2], early, mid and wants.foe[1]; 'Soulflare' is used as the name of the Mantra-empowered Q; and the packet flags that the page carries zero cooldown-sequencing advice.
audit.why: Riot's text for Smoke Screen is a cloud that reduces sight range plus an impact slow — it does not cause miss chance, and the mirror already corrected the same error. Quickdraw is 16/15/14/13/12s and its cooldown is lowered by his basic attacks, which is the number that makes 'step up on its downtime' actionable. End of the Line detonates on terrain, so he can drop it behind you and Karma has no dash out.
audit.corrected: Every blind restated as sight cut plus slow; Quickdraw's 16s rank-1 timer written into winCon, the do's and spikes[2]; the End of the Line retreat cut added to the don'ts; Soulflare replaced with Mantra-Q.
sources: kit: Graves W 'reduces sight range', cd 26/24/22/20/18

edits.before: You drift toward utility now — peel, shield, and speed your carries while the RQ poke softens objectives.
edits.after: Graves fades as a solo threat — Mantra-E shields, Mantra-W heals, and your roams decide the fights now.

edits.before: He brings his E dash and Smoke Screen online to close my range and blind me, so the trades start to even out around levels 3-6.
edits.after: Quickdraw closes range and Smoke Screen cuts your sight and slows — it is not a blind — so trades even out from level 3 on.

edits.before: Drop Smoke Screen on top of you so the blind and slow cover his step-up and your trade falls short
edits.after: Drop Smoke Screen on you so the sight cut and slow cover his step-up and your trade falls short

edits.before: His window: E dash plus Smoke Screen let him collapse range and drop a blind/slow zone, then his burst shotgun autos out-trade you point-blank while True Grit armor tanks your Q.
edits.after: His window: Quickdraw (16s at rank 1) plus Smoke Screen collapse range and cut your sight, then his burst shotgun autos out-trade you point-blank while True Grit armour tanks your Q.

edits.before: Keep Q on his head — every ability and auto that lands refunds Mantra off your passive (Gathering Fire), so you rebuild Soulflare faster than his short-range autos can punish a step-up.
edits.after: Keep Q on his head — every ability and auto that lands refunds Mantra off your passive (Gathering Fire), so you re-empower faster than his short-range autos can punish a step-up.

edits.before: Out-poke the poker and shield the difference. Nothing here works through Quickdraw — schedule your pattern around its cooldown.
edits.after: Out-poke the poker and shield the difference. Step up only when Quickdraw is down — 16s at rank 1 — and root him as he lands.

edits.before: Dash + armor stacks — burst him after the charges are spent. Commit on its cooldown, never into it.
edits.after: Quickdraw is 16s at rank 1 and refunds off his autos — burst him once the dash and armour are spent.

edits.before: E is your only defensive button — spending it on poke speed leaves you naked to the full engage.
edits.after: End of the Line detonates on terrain and can cut your retreat — you have no dash, so hold Flash for it.

notes: spikes[0].text and the early/mid/late prose still contain 'Soulflare' and first-person voice; I converted only what I edited, so a voice-and-name sweep is still owed on this matchup. Note also that Karma's Q, Graves' Q, W, R and his passive bullets are all flagged as projectiles, but neither champion has a projectile-blocking tool, so nothing was written about it.
